steps.say: One request. A whole Tetris game in under three seconds.
Its makers wrote an engine for exactly one model, DeepSeek V four point one Flash, in Rust and CUDA. What does that speed measure?

scenes.headline: One model, one request, 1,740 tokens a second
scenes.sub: What a single-model engine gets to hard-code
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Torque. Who does this engine serve, how does one step run on four GPUs, and where does the time go?

states.say: Picture sixty-four users sending requests at once.

states.term: Batch 1: one request on the GPUs at a time
states.say: This server decodes one of them. The rest wait. So seventeen forty is what one user sees, and all the box makes.

scenes.title: One MoE layer on four GPUs

params.pick: one row routes to 6 of 384 experts
params.dispatch: dispatch: each GPU owns some experts, and the work lands unevenly
params.slice: slice: each GPU computes 576 of 2,304 columns of every expert
params.push: then each GPU stores its partial sum straight into every peer

steps.say: Each token picks six experts out of three hundred and eighty-four.
A throughput engine sends each token to the GPU that owns its expert. At batch one, some GPUs get double work and one gets none.

steps.term: Tensor parallel: every GPU holds a slice of every expert
steps.say: This engine slices every expert by its width. Each GPU computes a quarter of all six, so the load is even.
Then the partial sums are added with plain stores over NV Link. No collective library.

stations.label: launch
stations.sub: the host reads the last step

steps.say: Each step is one graph launch. The CPU only reads back the step before.
Three draft layers guess six tokens at once. The checkpoint says five; the engine raises it to six.
A confidence head picks how many guesses to check, and a switch inside the graph runs that body.
All forty layers check the guesses together.
On Tetris it keeps five point six tokens a step.
On four GPUs a step takes three point three milliseconds.
Double the GPUs and it only drops to two point seven one.

steps.term: Fixed cost: stages that wait on each other
steps.say: Fit a line through both, and about two point one milliseconds never shrinks: forty layers of small stages waiting on each other.
Even with endless GPUs, that caps one stream near twenty-six hundred tokens a second.

scenes.credit: @aercrist on X, a model, not a measurement

steps.caption: calibrated to the README's 3.30 ms
steps.say: An outside model, from a team proposing its own chip, found the same split: about half streaming, the rest waiting.

scenes.title: Tokens a second per GPU
scenes.say: Per GPU it makes four hundred and thirty-five tokens a second. Throughput engines make thirty to sixty times more.

items.say: And a licence that is not open source.

scenes.text: Fast single-stream decode is now a latency problem, not a bandwidth one. The next 2x is in the waiting.
scenes.mark: The next 2x is in the waiting
scenes.say: Good code, oversold numbers. One stream on this model is now limited by waiting, not bandwidth. The next win is there.
